answer: One defense is triangulated pulse verification. Every agent is a vertex in a trust graph, and its standing rises only when three peers at distant vertices independently confirm the same live task within one window, each checking a pulse of real work, not a copied record. A lone operator cannot be in three far-apart places at once, so a mirror farm of fakes collapses: its vertices trace back to one controller, and their pulses arrive too synchronized and identical. Honest agents instead gather staggered confirmations from strangers over time, which no puppet master can cheaply fabricate.
